experiments.title: Pulley sections
experiments.instruction: Choose Pulley sections. Predict what happens to ideal pulling force and rope travel. Select a prediction, then Set baseline and Use two sections. Keep the load at 40 kg and lift it 0.5 m. Change only the supporting rope sections from one to two.
experiments.observe: Ideal pulling force falls from 392.4 N to 196.2 N; rope travel rises from 0.5 m to 1.0 m. Ideal input work and the load's gravitational energy gain are both 196.2 J. Explain why less force requires more rope.

experiments.title: Gear ratio
experiments.instruction: Choose Gear ratio. Predict what happens to crank turns and ideal hand force at the crank. Select a prediction, then Set baseline and Use 48 driven teeth. Keep the 12-tooth driver, 40 kg load, 0.5 m lift and 0.20 m crank and drum radii fixed. Change only the driven gear from 12 to 48 teeth.
experiments.observe: Crank turns rise from 0.40 to 1.59 while ideal hand force falls from 392.4 N to 98.1 N. The fixed load and drum still require 78.48 N·m output torque; at 4:1 that is four times the 19.62 N·m input torque. Ideal work stays 196.2 J.
